prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.sub: The rules that decide what reaches your feed. Your profile's rules are yours to rewrite; the shared ones hold the machinery and are read-only.
prompts.readonly_note: Shared rules: the output format, the clustering and gate questions. They show how the scoring works. A broken file costs a whole run, so you cannot edit it here.
prompts.pick_left: Pick a prompt on the left
prompts.test_hint: Scores a past run's signals with what is in the box. One call, nothing is saved.
prompts.test_source_sample: Tested against the sample run shipped with the app. Do your own run for your own signals.
prompts.test_caveat: The log stores no star counts, so traction rules cannot be reproduced here. A score also depends on the whole batch, so this answers "did my rule fire", not "this is the next run".
profiles.confirm_delete: Delete the profile "{name}" and its prompt? Topics already saved are not touched.
settings.title: Settings
settings.sub: Your keys and your X session. They stay on this machine, in a .env file beside the app.
settings.github_help: Needs no scopes at all, public search works with a bare token. github.com → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens.
settings.openai_help: Scoring costs roughly $0.10 per run on the default model. platform.openai.com → API keys.
settings.model_help: The app is built around a small cheap model. The pipeline tolerates its mistakes, so a pricier one buys you nothing.
settings.unchanged_hint: Leave a field empty to keep what is already saved.
settings.x_help: Optional. Without it the app runs on GitHub only. Anyone holding this file can act as your X account, and it never leaves this machine.
settings.cookies_ph: Paste the Cookie-Editor export here (a JSON array)
settings.cookies_steps: Install the Cookie-Editor extension, open x.com logged in, press Export → JSON, and paste it here.
wizard.title: Let's get you set up
wizard.intro: This app scans GitHub and X and gives you a ranked list of topics to write about. A few short steps and it is yours.
wizard.done_help: Open the Feed, pick your sources and press Run. The first run takes a few minutes, mostly reading X.
status.profile_no_sources: Profile {name} has no sources. Add them on the Profiles tab
prompts.about._base: The shared base for every profile: what counts as noise, the reply format, and the language of the description. It is prepended to the profile rules on every scoring call.
prompts.about._group: The second call. Merges signals about the same event into one topic, so a single announcement does not become three cards.
prompts.about._xgate: The tweet gate. It asks one thing: is there a raw fact left to build your own post on, or did the author already say everything. It never touches repositories.
prompts.about._feedgate: The official-source gate. It asks one thing: is this post the event itself, or the company talking about itself. Customer case studies, awards and how-tos for the publisher's own product are dropped. It never touches repositories or tweets.
prompts.about._dedup: The last call. Drops topics whose story you already saw in an earlier run, even when the links differ.
prompts.about._meta: The text you hand to ChatGPT or Claude so it interviews you and writes a profile's rules. It is what the guide's button copies. The pipeline never reads this file.
prompts.confirm_discard: Close the editor? Unsaved changes will be lost.
prompts.confirm_restore: Restore the previous version? The current text becomes the backup, so this can be undone.
prompts.guide_title: How to write your own prompt
prompts.guide_s1: Press "Copy for an LLM". The clipboard gets a ready-made text that asks the LLM to interview you.
prompts.guide_s2: Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude and answer its questions: what you write about, who reads you, what you are tired of seeing.
prompts.guide_s3: Once it has asked enough, it hands back a finished rules file as one block.
prompts.guide_s4: Press Edit, paste those rules over what is here, and save.
prompts.guide_s5: Press Test to see how the new rules score the last run's signals. If it is worse, restore the previous version.
profiles.confirm_discard: Leave this screen? Unsaved profile changes will be lost.
settings.tuning_help: How wide to cast the net and how strictly to judge. Applies from the next run, no restart needed.
tune.SCORE_THRESHOLD_help: What a signal must score to become a topic. Higher means fewer topics, better picked.
tune.GH_PER_PAGE_help: Repos fetched per tag. This is the width of the net, not its strictness: more costs more but softens nothing. Maximum 100.
tune.X_MAX_TWEETS_help: Tweets scraped from each account, list and search. More means a longer run and a dearer scoring pass.
tune.GH_FRESH_DAYS_help: A repo untouched for longer than this never enters a run.
tune.X_FRESH_DAYS_help: Tweets older than this are dropped before scoring.
tune.TREND_MIN_VELOCITY_help: The growth rate that puts a repo into the breakout section.
tune.TRACK_STAGNANT_DAYS_help: A repo that has not grown for this long leaves Tracked, star history and all.
tune.OFF_INTEREST_help: Subjects dropped before scoring, comma separated. Matches the name or the start of the description, so a tool that merely lists them among supported models survives. Empty means drop nothing.
settings.reset_help: Removes shown topics, the watchlist, the star history and banned repos. A copy is left beside it as topics.db.backup. Keys, profiles and prompts are untouched.
settings.wipe_sub: Tick what to remove. A copy of the database stays in topics.db.backup.
settings.wipe_topics_help: The record of what you have already seen. Clear it and old topics can reach the feed again.
settings.wipe_tracked_help: The repo list and every star measurement. Growth rates start accumulating from zero again.
settings.wipe_banned_help: The repos you threw out. After this they can reach a run again.
settings.wipe_confirm: Delete: {parts}? This cannot be undone, only topics.db.backup will remain.
